chapter: Charley Johnson and the Army band
title: Bugle Blues copied from the Fifteenth Regiment
summary: The band played Sousa marches and tried to copy Jim Europe's Fifteenth Regiment band's Bugle Blues.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: But, what kind of music did you play? Of course, you played marches, but did you play anything else?

Oh yeah, Sousa marches, and then they started -- we tried to imitate, one thing that we tried to imitate was Jim Europe, at the Fifteenth, they had a fellow named Fats. And Fats played -- from Chicago -- and he played this "Bugle Blues." That's the first time I heard the Bugle Blues, and

so -- but I know some fellows later on have claimed that they originated the 'Bugle Blues', but they didn't. It was originated in the Army, in the Fifteenth Regiment. And, see, we tried to copy it from them because we had a chance to hear them once. We played it, we was the only outfit that played guard mount for the Marines. We was connected with the First Army Headquarters and the -- and we had some awful experiences over there because -- one of the experiences we had, the boys got kind of gay one time, so they gave us some saltpetre, and all the guys got diarrhea.
